prompt: In Experiment 1, which factor was deliberately set to different values by the experimenters?

choices.rationale: Correct. The temperature of the water was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The purity of the water was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The shape of the beaker is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

choices.text: The mass of salt that dissolved
choices.rationale: The mass of salt that dissolved was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).

explanation: The procedure changes the temperature of the water from trial to trial and records the mass of salt that dissolved in response, so the temperature of the water is the independent variable.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students heated 100 g of distilled water to a set temperature in a beaker and added the salt one gram at a time, stirring after each addition, until no more would dissolve. They recorded the total mass dissolved at each temperature. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following was the dependent variable (the variable measured as the outcome)?

choices.rationale: The color of the bob is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
Correct. The period of the pendulum was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
The length of the string was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The type of string was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

explanation: The period of the pendulum is what the experimenters measured after setting the length of the string, so it is the dependent variable.

stimulus.title: Pendulum Period
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
Students hung a metal bob from a string, pulled the bob 10° to one side, and released it. They timed 10 complete swings with a stopwatch and divided by 10 to find the period. The procedure was repeated for several string lengths.
Results (the period of the pendulum): at 20 cm, 0.90 s; at 40 cm, 1.27 s; at 60 cm, 1.56 s; at 80 cm, 1.80 s; at 100 cm, 2.01 s.

prompt: To make the trials of Experiment 1 comparable, the experimenters most likely kept which of the following the same?

choices.rationale: The time of day is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
The altitude of the station was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).

choices.text: The boiling point of the water
choices.rationale: The boiling point of the water was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
Correct. The kettle and thermometer was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

explanation: Only the altitude of the station was varied and only the boiling point of the water was measured; the kettle and thermometer was kept the same so it could not affect the results.

table.caption: Experiment 1: A team carried the same kettle, thermometer, and a measured volume of distilled water to stations at several altitudes. At each station the water was heated until it boiled steadily and the temperature was recorded. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: Why did the experimenters most likely include a trial at an antibiotic concentration of 0 µg/mL?

choices.text: Serve as a control against which the other trials could be compared
choices.rationale: Correct. A zero trial shows what happens with none of the treatment, so the effect of each nonzero amount can be judged against it.

choices.text: Determine whether the volume of culture spread on each plate has any effect on the number of colonies
choices.rationale: The volume of culture spread on each plate was held constant, so no trial can test its effect.

choices.text: Check that the instrument used to measure the number of colonies was properly calibrated
choices.rationale: Nothing in the procedure uses the zero trial to calibrate an instrument.

choices.text: Produce the largest possible value of the number of colonies in the experiment
choices.rationale: The 0 µg/mL row is a baseline, not an attempt to obtain a maximum.

explanation: A trial with antibiotic concentration of zero serves as the control: it establishes the baseline value of the number of colonies against which the other trials are compared.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students spread 0.1 mL of a bacterial culture onto agar plates containing a known concentration of an antibiotic. After 24 hours they counted the colonies on each plate. Three plates were prepared for each concentration and the average count was recorded. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: Which variable did the experimenters intentionally vary from trial to trial in Experiment 1?

choices.rationale: The location of the boat was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The water temperature was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
Correct. The depth below the surface was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The color of the boat is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

explanation: The procedure changes the depth below the surface from trial to trial and records the water temperature in response, so the depth below the surface is the independent variable.

table.caption: Experiment 1: From a boat anchored over the deepest part of a lake, students lowered a thermometer probe on a marked cable and recorded the water temperature at several depths. All readings were taken within one hour at midday. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: Which quantity was measured as the result of each trial in Experiment 1?

choices.rationale: The mass of catalyst was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The volume of hydrogen peroxide was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

choices.text: The time for the reaction to finish
choices.rationale: Correct. The time for the reaction to finish was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
The brand of the stopwatch is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

explanation: The time for the reaction to finish is what the experimenters measured after setting the mass of catalyst, so it is the dependent variable.

stimulus.title: Catalyst and Reaction Time
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
Students mixed 50 mL of hydrogen peroxide solution from a single bottle with a measured mass of powdered catalyst and timed how long it took for the bubbling to stop.
Results (the time for the reaction to finish): at 0 mg, 183 s; at 2 mg, 97 s; at 4 mg, 54 s; at 6 mg, 34 s; at 8 mg, 24 s.

prompt: To make the trials of Experiment 1 comparable, the experimenters most likely kept which of the following the same?

choices.rationale: The color of the bob is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
The period of the pendulum was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).

choices.text: The angle from which the bob was released
choices.rationale: Correct. The angle from which the bob was released was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The length of the string was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).

explanation: Only the length of the string was varied and only the period of the pendulum was measured; the angle from which the bob was released was kept the same so it could not affect the results.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students hung a metal bob from a string, pulled the bob 10° to one side, and released it. They timed 10 complete swings with a stopwatch and divided by 10 to find the period. The procedure was repeated for several string lengths. Table 1 lists the results.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students wrapped a metal box containing an electric heater in foam sheets of a set total thickness. They adjusted the heater power until the inside temperature held steady in a 20°C room and recorded that power as the rate of heat loss. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following was the independent variable (the variable the experimenters deliberately changed)?

choices.rationale: The brand of paper towel is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
Correct. The soaking time was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).

choices.text: The percent of seeds that sprouted
choices.rationale: The percent of seeds that sprouted was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).

choices.text: The number of days allowed for sprouting
choices.rationale: The number of days allowed for sprouting was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

explanation: The procedure changes the soaking time from trial to trial and records the percent of seeds that sprouted in response, so the soaking time is the independent variable.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students soaked batches of 50 radish seeds in water for a set number of hours, then placed each batch on damp paper towels in a covered tray. After 5 days they counted the seeds that had sprouted and converted the count to a percent. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: Which quantity was measured as the result of each trial in Experiment 1?

choices.rationale: Correct. The sound intensity was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).

choices.text: The height of the sound meter
choices.rationale: The height of the sound meter was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The distance from the speaker was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The brand of the speaker is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

explanation: The sound intensity is what the experimenters measured after setting the distance from the speaker, so it is the dependent variable.

stimulus.title: Distance and Sound Intensity
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
In an open field, students placed a speaker playing a steady tone and used a sound meter to measure the intensity at several distances along a straight line from the speaker. Readings were taken at the same height above the ground.
Results (the sound intensity): at 2 m, 26.6 µW/m²; at 3 m, 11.8 µW/m²; at 4 m, 6.6 µW/m²; at 5 m, 4.2 µW/m²; at 6 m, 3.0 µW/m².

prompt: To make the trials of Experiment 1 comparable, the experimenters most likely kept which of the following the same?

choices.rationale: The color of the pots is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
The height of the seedlings was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).

choices.text: The volume of solution given to each pot
choices.rationale: Correct. The volume of solution given to each pot was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The fertilizer concentration was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).

explanation: Only the fertilizer concentration was varied and only the height of the seedlings was measured; the volume of solution given to each pot was kept the same so it could not affect the results.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students planted bean seeds in identical pots of potting soil and watered each pot with 100 mL of fertilizer solution every other day. After 4 weeks they measured the height of each seedling. Each concentration was tested with five pots, and the average height was recorded. Table 1 lists the results.
